terms.grammar: complector, complectī, complexus sum, deponent, with accusative; in a relative clause, quī omnia complectitur
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.4.57: omnia alicujus facta ōrātiōne (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Brut. 14: omnium rērum memoriam breviter librō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Latin has no adjective for it: a comprehensive account is one that embraces everything, quae omnia complectitur. Complector is to embrace, and so to take in a subject whole, in thought or in a book.
Of the whole taken together, against its parts (ūniversa rēs, the whole subject); for a comprehensive view, not a comprehensive account.

phrases.latin: Hic liber omnia complectitur quae ad hortōs colendōs pertinent.
phrases.english: This book is comprehensive: it covers everything to do with gardening.

sources: Lewis & Short: complector · Lewis & Short: universus
